summary.overview: The project has substantive agent guidance and a rich project Memory base, but the hottest frontend code has no automated validation route, CI only runs at release time, and the guidance documents commands the manifest does not provide. Session behavior in the reviewed week was unobserved (two sessions, both self-analysis), so scores reflect inspected mechanisms only. Three exact Memory title collision groups are confirmed as metadata leads, with 12 near-title pairs deferred and conflict/staleness unobserved.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: Root guidance exists and routes agents to owners, but documented commands conflict with the package manifest and no task episode was observed to confirm intent handling.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Dev startup routes are named and partly runnable, while two documented commands fail and Rust tests require a manually pre-started proxy.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Inline Rust unit tests exist, but the frontend — the highest-churn area — has no test, lint, or typecheck route an agent can run after an edit.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: A release build pipeline exists, but nothing gates pull requests or ordinary pushes and the release build runs no tests.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: A bounded review completed and confirmed asset-integrity leads (duplicate skill copies, Memory title collisions), but no exercised loop or later-outcome evidence exists.

findings.title: Edits to the hottest frontend code have no runnable check
findings.reason: Fact: package.json exposes no test, lint, or typecheck script, the evidence pack counts zero frontend test files, and AGENTS.md itself states no lint or formatting config is committed. Inference: an agent editing the most-churned areas (src/pages, src/layout) gets no post-edit feedback, so regressions surface only at manual runtime use. Rust backend has inline unit tests, but they require a manually pre-started proxy. Owner: root package.json scripts plus a minimal frontend check configuration.
expectedOutput: One runnable post-edit check for frontend changes, documented truthfully in AGENTS.md.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest runnable frontend validation route for the hottest change areas (src/pages, src/layout). TypeScript is already a devDependency with a root tsconfig, so start with a typecheck script, then add a lint or focused test route only if it stays minimal. Update the AGENTS.md testing section to match what actually exists.

## Validation

- Run the new script from the repository root and confirm it exits cleanly on the current tree
- Confirm AGENTS.md documents only scripts present in package.json

findings.title: Changes reach release artifacts without any per-change gate
findings.reason: Fact: .github/workflows/build.yml triggers only on v* tags and workflow_dispatch, and its release build runs no tests, typecheck, or lint; docs-deploy.yml covers only the docs site. Inference: pull requests and ordinary pushes get no mechanical acceptance evidence, so agent or human changes are accepted on review prose alone. CI runtime status was not observed; the trigger configuration is the verified basis. Owner: .github/workflows plus the package.json scripts a check workflow would call.
expectedOutput: Every pull request runs the project's validation routes before merge, producing revision-bound acceptance evidence.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add one pull_request-triggered check workflow that runs the project's validation routes (the frontend typecheck/lint or test script and cd src-tauri && cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1 where feasible). Keep the existing release workflow untouched. Do not push, create branches, or open PRs; only add the workflow file locally.

## Validation

- Parse the new workflow (e.g. actionlint or a YAML check) and confirm it triggers on pull_request
- Confirm it invokes only scripts and commands that exist in package.json or AGENTS.md

findings.title: Agent guidance documents build commands that do not exist
findings.reason: Fact: AGENTS.md lists `pnpm build` and `pnpm preview` as standard commands, but package.json defines only dev, tauri, tauri:dev, dev:clean, docs, docs:dev, and deploy. Vite is present as a devDependency, so the capability exists but is not exposed as a script. Consequence: an agent following the sole entrypoint guidance hits script-not-found failures and must guess the replacement. Owner: AGENTS.md command list or package.json scripts.
expectedOutput: Every documented development command resolves to a real manifest script.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Reconcile the AGENTS.md Build, Test, and Development Commands section with package.json: either add build and preview scripts wrapping vite, or rewrite the documented commands to ones that actually exist. Keep the command list exactly in sync with the manifest.

## Validation

- Run each command listed in AGENTS.md against package.json scripts and confirm every one resolves
- If scripts were added, run them once and confirm they exit cleanly

findings.title: Two divergent impeccable skill copies share one name and version
findings.reason: Fact: .agents/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md and .qoder/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md both declare name impeccable and version 3.8.0, but the bodies differ: script paths point to different directories, invocation frontmatter differs (only one copy declares user-invocable and allowed-tools), and content blocks differ between copies. Inference: whichever copy loads yields different guidance from the same nominal skill, and any update must be applied twice or drift widens. No invocation evidence shows which copy is selected at runtime. Owner: project maintainer deciding one canonical copy.
expectedOutput: One unambiguous impeccable owner, so routing and future updates have a single target.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Choose one canonical impeccable installation (.qoder/skills or .agents/skills) and remove or archive the other so exactly one project-scope copy carries the name. Do not merge, rewrite, or edit skill content beyond removing the duplicate; confirm with the user before deleting either copy.

## Validation

- Confirm exactly one project-scope impeccable SKILL.md remains discoverable
- Confirm the surviving copy's script paths resolve to files that exist

findings.title: Oversized design skill loads fully and gives the router no task cue
findings.reason: Fact: the agent-lint profile flags the emil-design-eng skill at 679 lines over the length hard cap with no local Markdown references, and its description states what the skill is rather than when to use it. Consequence: every selection loads the full monolith at higher token cost, and the router has no task cue to match against, while four other design-surface skills compete for the same intent family (overlap inferred from names only, unverified). Owner: skill author.
expectedOutput: A trigger-matched, on-demand design skill instead of a full-load monolith.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Rework the emil-design-eng skill per the Progressive Disclosure rubric: move detailed guidance into reference Markdown files loaded on demand, and rewrite the frontmatter description as a use-when trigger. Do not change other skills in this pass.

## Validation

- Rerun the agent-assets lint and confirm the skill-length-hard-cap warning and the progressive-references advisory clear
- Confirm the description states the triggering task situation, not the skill's identity

findings.title: Project Memory title space carries exact collisions awaiting merge review
findings.reason: Fact: the integrity review over 338 project Memory titles found 3 exact same-scope title collision groups and 12 near-title similarity pairs (81-98%); titles were reviewed, bodies were not read and are out of authority. Disposition: exact collisions confirmed as metadata governance leads; near matches deferred; conflict/staleness and retrieval coverage unobserved. Titles without bodies prove neither duplicate content nor current impact. Owner: Memory maintainer performing bounded metadata review.
expectedOutput: Exact title collisions resolved or dispositioned, with near matches tracked as a remaining count.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Review only the 3 exact same-scope Memory title collision groups as metadata candidates: locate each pair with SearchMemory, judge same scope, and where bodies confirm duplication propose the merge through the update_memory route. Do not merge or delete without separate confirmation, and leave the 12 near-title pairs for a later bounded batch.

## Validation

- Confirm each reviewed pair is recorded as merged, distinct, or deferred with a reason
- Confirm no Memory body was modified without explicit approval
